# Conformance fixtures

Each directory holds a `log.jsonl` (a complete world log, genesis included)
and `folded.json` (the state the reference implementation folds it to).

**To check an implementation:** fold each log from empty state and compare
your result to `folded.json` — deep equality over exactly these fields:
`entities` (including each entity's `comp` bag and `parent`), `mounts`,
`roles`, `behaviors`. Chat windows, ban lists, and any other
implementation-defined folds are out of scope. Numbers compare within 1e-6
(orphan-stamping does trigonometry).

Notes per fixture:
- `01-build` — creation, transforms, lights, mount, and removal of a parent:
  the mounted child's absolute pose is computed and stamped (mug at
  table-pos + yaw-rotated offset).
- `02-swing` — the component story: sockets, reactions, an unknown component
  type that MUST survive, a motion written in generous dialect (`amplitude`,
  `axis: "x"`, no t0 — fold stamps `t0` from the entry), a `use` whose
  reaction emitted a world-authored motion with `{cause, by}` provenance,
  a body mounting and dismounting, and a final entry in a verb no
  implementation knows — which MUST fold to nothing and be kept.
- `03-authority` — first embodied joiner auto-owns a brand-new world;
  grants; the `*` wildcard (which can never be an owner).
- `04-overwrite` — the flat id namespace (§3.1, the 2026-08-09 erratum
  pinned): a same-id `spawn` replaces the previous holder WHOLESALE (its
  comp bag dies with it); a `light` on a model id and a `spawn` on a light
  id replace across kinds; `light`-on-`light` merges as a partial update
  (absent fields keep their prior values, `keep` folds in).
- `05-lightpolicy` — the light policy flags (§3.1): `keep` and `day` are
  stored only in their non-default state (`keep: true`, `day: false`),
  survive partial updates that don't mention them, and CLEAR back to
  absent when re-issued at the default (`day: true`, `keep: false`).
  Also: a comp and a mount land on a light and a later partial `light`
  keeps both — light-on-light merges, it does not re-author (§3.1, §4).

Fixtures 01–04 were generated by driving the reference sequencer over its
real websocket door (`/tmp` scratch worlds), not written by hand; 05's
`folded.json` is the shared fold's own output over its log — if you
disagree with one, one of us has a bug, and the argument will be short.

The reference implementation's own runner is `bun tools/foldfix-test.ts`,
which folds each fixture with `shared/fold.js` (the reference fold) and
applies exactly the comparison rule above.
